2. Learn how it makes its sound, one idea at a time.

## What it is

- The **Clavinet D6** came out in **1971** (Wikipedia, "Clavinet").
- Each key drives a rubber pad against a tensioned **steel string**, which sounds against an anvil point; an **electromagnetic pickup** turns the string's motion into a signal (Wikipedia).
- The other end of each string runs through **yarn**, which damps it as soon as the key is let go (Wikipedia). That is why it sounds so short and funky.

## Its sound

- Four tone rockers: **Brilliant** and **Treble** switch in a high-pass filter, **Medium** and **Soft** a low-pass filter (Wikipedia).
- Two rockers marked **AB** and **CD** choose the pickups (Wikipedia). Each pickup hears the string at a different place, so each is a different tone; which position is which pickup here is this page's reading (unverified).
- A **mute slider** on the right lays a damper on the strings (Wikipedia names it; how much it shortens the note is this page's).
- Hit harder and the string sounds louder and brighter: there is no sustain pedal (this page's model).

## The panel

The Clavinet's panel drawn after the real one (not a copy; no logos). Turn the knobs, flip the switches, play the keys below it,
the computer keys or a MIDI keyboard. **Simple** shows every control as a slider, including the adjustments inside the instrument.
The sound is this site's own physical model (see [how it is modelled](epiano-compare.qmd#how-each-one-is-modelled)); nobody has
compared it with the real instrument. Facts come from the Wikipedia articles listed under Works Cited (read 2026-11-26). The service manuals were not read for these pages, so control legends and places that Wikipedia does not give are marked unverified.

## A guided tour

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;}" data-riff="funk">

**Treble tab, upper pickup (C + A).** A sharp, bright funk riff.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;,&quot;pa&quot;:&quot;B&quot;}" data-riff="funk">

**Lower pickup (C + B).** The same riff: thinner and nasal, since the lower pickup sits nearer the string's end.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;,&quot;pc&quot;:&quot;D&quot;,&quot;pa&quot;:&quot;B&quot;}" data-riff="funk">

**Both pickups out of phase (D + B).** The low harmonics cancel: hollow and very thin.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;,&quot;treb&quot;:false,&quot;soft&quot;:true}" data-riff="funk">

**Soft tab.** A low-pass filter: round and dark.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;,&quot;mute&quot;:7}" data-riff="funk">

**Mute slider at 7.** Each note is cut short, like a muted guitar.

</div>

## Famous tracks

Each video was checked on YouTube (oEmbed, 2026-11-26). Listen first, then press **▶** for a starting setting on the panel above.

### "Use Me" (Bill Withers)

[▶ Bill Withers - Use Me (Official Audio)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NuYDKzky4z0) on YouTube (BillWithersVEVO).

Wikipedia names it. A two-note groove that never lets go: short, damped notes.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;,&quot;soft&quot;:false,&quot;treb&quot;:true,&quot;mute&quot;:3}" data-riff="funk">

**Starting setting** (Clavinet): soft False, treb True, mute 3. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "Higher Ground" (Stevie Wonder)

[▶ Higher Ground](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1esf0efHbjM) on YouTube (Stevie Wonder - Topic).

Wikipedia names it. A driving riff, thick and gritty (on the record also through effects: unverified).

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;clav&quot;,&quot;pc&quot;:&quot;D&quot;,&quot;pa&quot;:&quot;A&quot;,&quot;drive&quot;:6}" data-riff="funk">

**Starting setting** (Clavinet): pc D, pa A, drive 6. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

## Quiz

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What makes the sound of a Clavinet?</b></p><ul><li>A string struck against an anvil</li><li>A metal reed</li><li>A tine</li><li>A spring</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What do Brilliant and Treble switch in?</b></p><ul><li>A high-pass filter</li><li>A low-pass filter</li><li>A tremolo</li><li>A second string</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Why does a Clavinet note stop so fast?</b></p><ul><li>Yarn damps the string when the key is let go</li><li>The pickup turns off</li><li>The string breaks</li><li>A timer</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What are the AB and CD rockers for?</b></p><ul><li>Choosing the pickups</li><li>Changing octave</li><li>Turning on vibrato</li><li>Tuning</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
```
